glossary.definition: AI safety is the field focused on preventing AI systems from causing unintended harm, spanning near-term, everyday issues like biased hiring tools or misinformation, up to longer-term concerns about highly capable autonomous systems acting in ways nobody wanted. It's the same instinct as safety engineering in any powerful technology, cars, airplanes, nuclear power, just applied to software that can now make its own decisions.

items.title: Where was Nvidia’s security team?
items.summary: Nvidia’s security chief quietly left in August, and now that CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down over his relationships, including one with an executive at a company suspected of funneling chips to China, a former intelligence officer says it’s the kind of leak that runs everyday conversations, which most corporate security teams are poorly equipped to catch. Outsiders had little reason to notice when Nvidia’s longtime chief security officer and head of product security stepped down in August. S. investigators suspect of funneling Nvidia chips to China, then widening to reports about two separate affairs with Nvidia employees.

items.title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.summary: The petition had attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.

items.title: AT&T uses agentic AI to reinvent business processes from the ground up
items.summary: AT&T Corp. is moving beyond using artificial intelligence to improve employee productivity, increasingly applying autonomous agents to redesign how its business operates. Nearly 500 agentic workflows are already in production, and the telecom giant plans to triple that number next year. AT&T now processes about 45 billion AI tokens daily across the company, according to Luke Corbin (pictured, below), assistant vice president of digital transformation and AI at AT&T Business.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei admits "there's a huge uncertainty in what's going to happen next year" days before a record IPO
items.summary: Days before what could be the largest IPO in history, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called buying compute 'the deepest business dilemma' his company faces. Anthropic's commitments now total nearly $901 billion, and it's still far from clear whether future revenue will justify those costs. The planned IPO is largely meant to serve as a financial buffer against that uncertainty. Nobody knows how the company's compute investments will pay off, he says.

items.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
items.summary: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors.

items.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
items.summary: Fully automated ransomware hasn’t arrived—yet. But seemingly unsophisticated attackers are using AI tools to wreak havoc. With so much going on all the time, you may not have thought about ransomware and data extortion attacks in a minute, even though they’ve been among the the biggest cybersecurity threats to institutions—and, by extension, people—over the past decade. But in the new era of AI-powered and automated cyberattacks, the danger posed by ransomware is only increasing as cybercriminals profit by combining established methods with new techniques made possible or more accessible by AI.

items.title: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 6, 2025. | Photo by Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images On January 6th, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got his rockstar moment at last. He strode triumphantly onstage, hand raised in the air, to the claps and cheers of a 14,000-person arena absolutely packed with influencers and fans, their faces awash in blue glow, as he made his entrance in a black leather jacket that shimmered in the stadium's lights. Few are cheering for Jensen Huang now.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Exit Just Gave AMD and Google Their Biggest AI Opening
items.summary: On the same day that Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA’s chief executive after 33 years at the helm of the company he co-founded, another semiconductor company CEO was being celebrated. AMD CEO Lisa Su was named Yahoo Finance’s 2026 CEO of the Year. Su has had quite a triumphant year. AMD shares have been up nearly 139% year-to-date.

items.title: OpenAI Introduces ChatGPT Wallet for Agent-Led Payments
items.summary: OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a payment feature that allows AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users without accessing their actual card details. The feature requires users to approve every transaction through a security check, such as Face ID or fingerprint authentication. Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, ChatGPT Wallet will initially be available to ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and above in the US with eligible US-issued cards. The rollout will begin through OpenAI’s Dots personal agent.

items.title: Microsoft 365 services slowly come back online after global outage
items.summary: After a lengthy Microsoft 365 outage disrupted business around the globe, Microsoft is now restoring services to its customers. m. ET) on Friday, Nov. 13, Microsoft said that it is seeing broad recovery and stability across its services, although it is still reporting service degradation in Microsoft 365 services that interact with Exchange Online. “Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage.

items.title: Cloud reports measure the wrong thing
items.summary: Flexera’s 2026 State of the Cloud Report agrees with many other cloud reports these days: Cloud is more strategic, cloud is more complex, AI makes everything harder, and better governance is the answer. This report, based on a survey of 753 cloud decision-makers and users, argues that enterprise cloud has entered a “value era” in which organizations are measuring success less by cost savings alone and more by business outcomes. The headline findings are familiar. Flexera says 64% of organizations now use “value delivered to business units” as a metric for cloud progress, up 12 percentage points year over year.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s scandal-fueled ouster exposes enterprise doubts about AI
items.summary: The Nvidia shakeup probably won't damage the GPU giant, but it highlights risk lurking in the industry as enterprises deal with unclear ROI from AI technology.
